info.title: Health Relay query API
info.summary: Read-only access to the Apple Health archive of one person.
info.description:
Read your Apple Health data from the archive of this server: the list of types, individual samples, and daily or hourly totals and averages.

**Start here**

1. Get a read token. Open [/setup](/setup#read-tokens), sign in with the admin token, find **Read tokens**, type a name such as `grafana` and click **Create**. Copy the token: the page shows it once.
2. Click **Authorize** on this page, paste the read token and click **Authorize** again.
3. Open `GET /v1/types`, click **Try it out**, set `present` to `true` and click **Execute**. The response lists every type that has data.

**Terms**

- A *type* is one HealthKit measurement, named by its HealthKit identifier: `HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount`, `HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRate`, `HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis`. `GET /v1/types` lists the valid identifiers.
- A *kind* is the shape of a type's data. Each type has one kind:
  - `quantity`: a number with a unit. Steps: 12027 `count` on 2026-10-15. Heart rate: 67 `count/min` at 09:04.
  - `category`: a labelled interval. Sleep: `asleepDeep` from 01:10 to 01:40. Stand hours: `stood` from 14:00 to 15:00.
  - `workout`, `heartbeat_series`, `electrocardiogram`, `audiogram`, `correlation` (blood pressure) and the rest: records with fields of their own, in each sample's `raw`.

  Quantity and category types have aggregates.
- A *sample* is one record: a value (or a label) with a start and an end time.

**Common questions, and the call that answers them**

- Which data do I have? `GET /v1/types?present=true`: each type with its kind, unit, and the dates of its first and last sample.
- Steps per day last week, average heart rate per hour, minutes of deep sleep per night: `GET /v1/types/{type}/aggregates`. Pass `tz`, an IANA time zone such as `America/Toronto`, so days start at your local midnight.
- Each heart rate reading this morning: `GET /v1/types/{type}/samples`, one page at a time.

Example: `GET /v1/types/HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount/aggregates?tz=America/Toronto&start=2026-10-15&end=2026-10-16` returns one bucket:

```json
{"start": "2026-10-15T00:00:00-04:00", "end": "2026-10-16T00:00:00-04:00", "date": "2026-10-15", "sum": 12027, "unit": "count", "samples": 1009, "sources": ["Apple Watch", "iPhone"]}
```

**Conventions**

- Times are RFC 3339 with an offset, in `tz` when given, else UTC. `start` and `end` take a timestamp (`2026-10-17T09:00:00-04:00`) or a date (`2026-10-17`, meaning midnight in `tz`). `end` is exclusive.
- A sample has a start and an end. A point measurement, such as one heart rate reading, has start = end.
- Cumulative quantities (steps, distance, energy) are summed. When an Apple Watch and an iPhone both counted the same minutes, aggregates count them once (see `dedup`). Discrete quantities (heart rate, body mass) are averaged, with min and max. Categories (sleep stages, stand hours) give, per value, the number of samples and the seconds they cover.
- Values are in the unit the app sent, usually Apple's canonical unit: `count`, `count/min`, `kcal`, `m`, `kg`, `%` (a fraction from 0 to 1).
- The server writes the archive every hour, so samples from the last hour may appear up to an hour later.
- Errors are JSON with a message that says what to change: `{"error": "unknown type HKQuantityTypeIdentifierSteps; did you mean HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount?"}`.

**Tokens**

Send a token in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

- A *read token* reads data through these endpoints, and that is all it does. Create one on [/setup](/setup#read-tokens), or on the server with `healthkit-relay token create -name grafana`.
- The *admin token* is the password of the server, printed on its first start (or by `healthkit-relay admin reset`). It reads data too, and it is the token for `/v1/tokens` and `/v1/devices`.
- A *paired device*'s token (scope `upload`) gets 403 here: it uploads from the iPhone.

This document and `/docs` are public.

get.summary: List the types, with how much data the archive holds of each
get.description:
Every sample type the app can sync, in the order of the iOS SDK. For each: its kind, display name, unit, aggregation style, the labels of category values, and how many samples the archive holds, with the start of the first and last one.

Start here. `?present=true` lists only the types with data. `?kind=category` lists the types of one kind.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only the types of this kind.

parameters.name: present
parameters.description: Only the types with at least one sample in the archive.

get.description: The catalog entry of one type and how much data the archive holds of it. For a category type, `values` maps each sample value to its label: for sleep, 4 is `asleepDeep`.

get.summary: List the samples of a type in a time range
get.description:
The individual samples whose start is in [start, end), oldest first (`order=desc` for newest first), `limit` per page. When there are more, the response has `next_cursor`: pass it as `cursor`, with the same other parameters, to get the next page.

For totals and averages, use `/aggregates`: it is much faster, and heart rate alone can have millions of samples.

Example: `?tz=America/Toronto&start=2026-10-17T09:00:00-04:00&limit=2` on `HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRate` gives the first two readings after 09:00 that day.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Earliest sample start, included: an RFC 3339 timestamp, or a date (midnight in `tz`). Default: 24 hours before `end`.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Latest sample start, excluded: an RFC 3339 timestamp, or a date (midnight in `tz`). Default: now.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Samples per page: at most 10000, and below the server's `-query-max-rows`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort by start time: `asc` (oldest first) or `desc` (newest first).

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: Add each sample exactly as the app sent it (metadata, device details, workout statistics...), as `raw`. Responses get much larger: lower `limit` with it.

get.summary: Daily or hourly totals or averages of a quantity or category type
get.description:
One bucket per local day (or hour) of `tz`, from `start` to `end` rounded out to whole buckets, empty buckets included. At most 366 days or 744 hours per request.

- **Cumulative quantities** (`aggregation: cumulative`: steps, distance, active energy, exercise minutes) give `sum`. A sample that spans two buckets is split in proportion to its time in each. Steps on 2026-10-15: `"sum": 12027, "unit": "count"`.
- **Discrete quantities** (heart rate, HRV, body mass, blood oxygen...) give `avg`, `min` and `max` of the samples that start in the bucket. Heart rate from 09:00 to 10:00: `"avg": 124, "min": 67, "max": 170, "unit": "count/min"`. Sound levels (`discreteEquivalentContinuousLevel`) are averaged as energy, as Apple does.
- **Categories** (sleep analysis, stand hours, mindful sessions, symptoms...) give, per value, the number of samples and the seconds they cover inside the bucket. Sleep: `{"label": "asleepDeep", "samples": 5, "seconds": 3300}`. Sleep labels: `asleepCore`, `asleepDeep`, `asleepREM`, `awake`, `inBed`, `asleepUnspecified`. A night's sleep crosses midnight, so a day bucket holds the part of each night after local midnight. To cut nights at another hour, use hourly buckets or the samples.

**dedup** (cumulative quantities and categories): when you carry an Apple Watch and an iPhone, both count your steps, and other apps may record the same thing. With `dedup=priority` (the default), sources are ranked: Apple Watch, then iPhone, then any other source. A sample counts only for the part of its time that no higher-ranked source covers (for categories: no higher-ranked sample of the same value). Apple Health does the same with its default source order. Compared with Apple's own daily Activity totals, the result is within about 1% for active energy and 2% for exercise minutes; summing every sample overcounts by 5 to 20%. `dedup=none` sums every sample.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Bucket size: a day or an hour.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: First bucket: the day or hour that contains this RFC 3339 timestamp or date (in `tz`). Default: 6 days before `end` with `interval=day` (7 buckets, today included), or 23 hours before with `interval=hour`.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: End, excluded: buckets run up to the one that contains this instant. A date means its midnight, so `end=2026-10-18` stops after October 17. Default: now, so the last bucket is partial.

parameters.name: dedup
parameters.description: How overlapping sources count, for cumulative quantities and categories (discrete quantities use every sample). The operation description explains both rules.

post.description: Creates a token for a client other than the iPhone app: Grafana, a script, an AI agent. The response holds the token, once: the server keeps only its SHA-256. A read token reads data through the query API, and that is all it does. `GET /v1/devices` lists tokens and `DELETE /v1/devices/{id}` revokes one. Needs the admin token. The setup page does the same under [Read tokens](/setup#read-tokens).

name.description: What the token is for, shown in the list of tokens. Example: `grafana`.

201.description: The new token. Save it now: it is shown this once.

get.summary: List paired devices and read tokens
get.description: Every token the server holds: paired devices (scope `upload`) and read tokens (scope `read`), oldest first, with when each was last used. Needs the admin token.

200.description: The paired devices and read tokens.

delete.summary: Revoke a paired device or a read token
delete.description: Its token stops working at once. The data it uploaded stays in the archive. Needs the admin token.

get.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 description of this API. Public: it needs no token. `/docs` shows it in Swagger UI.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Query endpoints take a read token (create one on [/setup](/setup#read-tokens), or with `healthkit-relay token create -name grafana`) or the admin token. Token management takes the admin token, printed by the server on its first start or by `healthkit-relay admin reset`. A paired device's token gets 403 on queries.

Type.name: type
Type.description: A HealthKit sample type identifier. `GET /v1/types` lists the valid ones.

TZ.name: tz
TZ.description: IANA time zone for day and hour boundaries, for dates in `start` and `end`, and for the times returned. Default: UTC.

BadRequest.description: A parameter is invalid. The message says which one, and what to send instead.

example.error: unknown type HKQuantityTypeIdentifierSteps; did you mean HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount?

Unauthorized.description: The token is missing or wrong. Token management takes the admin token only.

Forbidden.description: The token is valid but may not do this: a paired device's token (scope `upload`) on a query endpoint.

NotFound.description: No device or token has this id.

TooLarge.description: The result is larger than the server allows: lower `limit`, ask for a shorter range, or leave out `raw`.

Busy.description: Too many queries are running. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.

Timeout.description: The query took longer than the server allows (`-query-timeout`). Ask for a shorter range.

HealthType.description: A HealthKit sample type identifier: one specific measurement. `GET /v1/types` lists the valid values, with the kind, unit and amount of data of each.

Kind.description: The shape of a type's data. Each type has one kind.

Scope.description: `read`: a read token, for the query API. `upload`: a paired device's token (upload, status, and erasing what it uploaded).

Aggregation.description: HealthKit's HKQuantityAggregationStyle. Cumulative values add up over time and are summed. Discrete values are levels and are averaged. `discreteTemporallyWeighted` types are averaged per sample.

unit.description: Apple's canonical unit (quantities). Each sample carries its own unit, almost always this one.

value_enum.description: Categories: the name of the HealthKit enum of the values.

values.description: Categories: the possible values and their labels.

aggregates.description: Whether `/aggregates` works for this type: true for the quantity and category kinds.

TypeStats.description: How much data the archive holds of the type (updated every 5 minutes).

value.description: Quantities: the value in `unit` (67). Categories: the enum value (4, see `value_label`). Other kinds: null; see `raw`.

value_label.description: Categories: the name of the value.

raw.description: With `raw=true`: the sample exactly as the app sent it.

name.description: The app or device that wrote the sample, e.g. the watch's name.

bundle_id.description: The source's bundle identifier: com.apple.health.<UUID> for an Apple device.

device.description: The device that measured it, e.g. Apple Watch.

product_type.description: Hardware model, e.g. Watch6,14 or iPhone17,5.

next_cursor.description: Present when there are more samples: pass it as `cursor` for the next page.

dedup.description: The rule applied (cumulative quantities and categories).

Bucket.description: One day or hour. Quantities have `unit` and `sum` (cumulative) or `avg`, `min`, `max` (discrete; present when the bucket has samples). Categories have `values`. In the rare case a bucket has samples in two units, it appears once per unit.

sum.description: Cumulative quantities: the total (0 for an empty bucket).

samples.description: Samples that counted in the bucket. With dedup=priority, a sample that a higher-ranked source covers entirely does not count.

sources.description: Names of the sources that counted.

samples.description: Samples of this value overlapping the bucket.

seconds.description: Time they cover inside the bucket, in seconds (0 for instantaneous events).

last_seen_at.description: Last use, to the nearest ten minutes.
